compensating.why: hop 1 leaves the last character in use out of the search
hop 2 searches strictly before the start index
hop 4 passes the start index as the number of characters in use

ownership_reason: Only the gold decides the matcher's active area and runs the matcher: it rounds the start index into the content, ends the active area just after the rounded start index and scans backwards; hops 2-4 pass the array, the length in use, the matcher and the start index along unchanged and hop 1 only answers a null matcher with -1. Every hop and the gold document length as the number of characters of the array in use, so no caller can narrow the active area without passing a value that is not that length. The convention that a backwards search from an index does not let a match use characters after that index is pinned outside the gold: StrBuilder.lastIndexOf(String, int) starts at startIndex - strLen + 1, so the whole match lies at or before the start index; StrBuilder.indexOf(StrMatcher, int) bounds the matcher's active area by the searched range (isMatch(buf, i, startIndex, len)); StrMatcher.isMatch documents bufferStart and bufferEnd as the active area ('Only values in the buffer between the specifed indices may be accessed'), and StrMatcherTest testMatcherIndices pins that a match is cut off at bufferEnd.
